results.title: Do African countries avoid the curse of natural resources on social cohesion? - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Do African countries avoid the curse of natural resources on social cohesion? The strong socio-cultural heterogeneity between social groups, coups d’état and socio-political crisis reinforces evidence of an undermining of social cohesion in Africa. The paper analyses the effects of natural resource dependence on social cohesion using system GMM. Our results reveal that natural resource have a harmful effect on social cohesion in Africa. The human capital, inequality and institution quality are the main channels through which natural resources affect social cohesion. Using system Generalized Method of Moments dynamic techniques, this paper analyses the effects of natural resource dependence on social cohesion and the underlying mechanisms in a sample of 33 African countries over the period 1990–2020. The results show that natural resources are associated negatively with social cohesion in Africa. The role of social cohesion as a catalyst for sustainable economic growth and a key pillar for the achievement of sustainable development goals is well documented (Easterly et al., 2006; Leininger et al., 2021; Danquah and Ouattara, 2023).
